raw_signal: (no owner signal -- this came out of a macro pass)
observations: Across a whole commit the application makes exactly ONE network request: `GET /assets/ValueReconstruction-*.js`, at +2417ms.

Serving that one URL a 404 -- the exact deploy case `lazy-chunk.ts` names -- at 1440x900: +76ms the commitment panel is gone and `aria-busy=1`; +2554ms THE REVEAL RENDERS (body innerText 860 -> 1550); +2610ms `document.body.innerText.length = 0` and `scrollHeight = 0`; +2697ms the app is remounting; +2764ms the DECIDE screen. The reveal is present in one 50ms sample and the document is empty in the next.
Aborting the same URL instead of 404ing it produces the identical shape. Reproduced 4x across both injection kinds, 8 runs in total.

It is the product's own path and not the probe's: the app POSTs `/api/client-event` with `{"code":"stale-build-reload","failureClass":"stale-build"}` and writes the `decision-lab.chunk-reload` sessionStorage mark. `lazy-chunk.ts` retries once, then calls `window.location.reload()`.

WHERE THE RELOAD LANDS. The position committed on and the position put back are the same: h1 `11. O-O-O` and a 64-square occupancy hash of -494095640 on both sides. The commitment panel is reset to `חסרים 4 פרטים. החלטה חלקית לא נרשמת`, the record reads `0 מתוך 1 שנרשמו`, and a second full decision was then committed on that same position with the same move.
ON REVEAL 1 THE CHUNK PAINTS NOTHING. `ASK_AFTER_REVEALS = 2`, so the component mounts, fetches, and renders nothing until the second reveal -- and still costs the first one.

THE FIRST FAILURE IS SILENT. The product has a well-written stale-build screen -- `האפליקציה התעדכנה בזמן שהייתם כאן ... החלטות שכבר נרשמו נשמרו` with a reload control -- and it appears only on the SECOND failure.
The same class at the disclosure: aborting `/assets/RecordExplorer-*.js` at the `.explore-toggle` press empties the document at +110ms and lands the DECIDE screen at +357ms, reveal gone.

THE ENVIRONMENT DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT AVAILABLE, and that is a finding about the finding. `/api/client-event` calls `emit`, which writes one JSON line through `sink` -- a runtime log. `MASTER_PRODUCT_DEBT`/`PRE_HUMAN_CEILING` item `R-23` records what that means here: Vercel Hobby retains runtime logs for ONE HOUR and sends no alerts, so the event is observable only by an operator who is already looking. Counting `stale-build-reload` events near reveal renders cannot be done retrospectively at all.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The reload is safe and the reveal is expendable
candidate_mechanisms.explains: `lazy-chunk.ts`'s own docblock, which argues safety on two legs: the record is written per decision, and `session-position` puts the board back.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: That both legs were measured and both hold, and neither of them is the reveal. The docblock does not mention it. The reveal is the one thing the product exists to produce and the only screen this component can mount on.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The placement is harmless because the trigger never fires there
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Why this has not been seen. The trigger is a deploy replacing a chunk while a page is open.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: Nothing measured contradicts it, and `lazy-chunk.ts` calls the trigger 'not hypothetical and not rare'.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: ENVIRONMENT, and it is BLOCKED. The app already emits the event, but it emits it into a one-hour log with no alerting (`R-23`), so the count cannot be taken retrospectively. `R-23` is itself an open OWNER decision -- buy retention and alerting, or accept the blindness and say so -- and this question is downstream of it. A trial that runs while nobody is watching cannot answer it either.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The reload is the wrong recovery for a screen holding unpersisted state
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Everything measured, and why the same shape appears at the disclosure with a different chunk.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: OWNER for the shape of the repair; the observation needs none.

design_distinction: A recovery that is safe for the RECORD is not automatically safe for the SCREEN. `lazy-chunk.ts` proved the first and was read as having proved the second, and the difference is exactly the state that is derived rather than stored.
authority: REPO for the observation and the mechanism, both measured. ENVIRONMENT for how often the trigger fires. OWNER for whether the reveal must survive the recovery, and for the shape of any repair. FIELD for what losing a reveal costs a player.
must_not_change: The reload itself, until the owner has answered. It exists because a stale build serving a missing chunk is a real deploy state, and removing the recovery to protect one screen would trade a rare lost reveal for a permanently broken page.
perceptual_success_criterion: A player who has just been shown a verdict is not returned, silently, to the position they took it on.
check: The eight runs above, both injection kinds, at 1440x900. The app's own `stale-build-reload` event and its sessionStorage mark are what distinguish the product's reload from the harness's.
next_step: The order of operations changed once the discriminator was checked. (1) `R-23` first: the frequency question is not answerable in a one-hour log with no alerting, so the cheap route is shut until that owner decision is made. (2) Only then, or independently if the owner prefers: if the reveal must survive the recovery, three shapes exist -- move the mount off the reveal, fold those four lines into the entry chunk, or defer the reload until the screen holds nothing a reload destroys -- and which is right is product intent. None is chosen here. Note that folding into the entry would fix one chunk and not the mechanism: the same shape was measured at the disclosure with `RecordExplorer`.
related: N-9. This is the third route into a re-armed already-decided position, and the most damaging one, because the player also loses the reveal. The reading half is already protected: the between-player comparison admits one answer per bank position.
